historical_record.description: A three-storey bottling warehouse was built as an extension of the Schilling winery, sharing a wall with it.

A concrete tank building was added north of the winery, the last of four wood-frame and concrete additions put up from 1912; the shipping room, the storage warehouse and the brandy house were the others.
Schilling and the firms that succeeded it left the site, which they had occupied since the winery was built.

Fire destroyed the inside of the winery. It was rebuilt to match with salvaged timbers, so little of the framing and finish inside was original afterwards; the warehouse interior survived largely intact.

Esprit, on the site since 1972, turned the storage room and brandy house into a design studio and executive offices and put steel industrial windows along the north front. It had already emptied the tank building of its tanks and made it a kitchen and store.
Esprit left after thirty-one years and the buildings stood empty.
Six buildings totaling approximately 144,000 square feet, the C. Schilling & Co. Wine Cellars complex, stood at the property.

The City Planning Commission approved the certification of the Final Environmental Impact Report for the 900 Minnesota Street project, which proposes to demolish four buildings, partially demolish and rehabilitate a fifth building, alter and rehabilitate a sixth building, and construct four new buildings with up to 142 dwelling units.

The City Planning Commission approved the adoption of CEQA findings for the 900 Minnesota Street project, which requests conditional use authorization for residential dwelling units and a Planned Unit Development.

The City Planning Commission approved the determination that the net new shadow on Esprit Park caused by the construction of the residential development at 900 Minnesota Street will not be significant or adverse.
Locked-out Jung Sai garment workers picketed the Esprit company's premises here, in buildings since replaced; 38 demonstrators were arrested.
